title: Transboundary haze FAQs
summary: The page sets out health advice during haze, including who is most affected, indoor measures, when N95 masks are and are not needed, and what to do for each 24-hour PSI band.

title: Managing haze
summary: The page says health effects depend on the PSI level, a person's health and time spent outdoors, and sets out how activity advice changes across the PSI bands.

title: Haze
summary: The page gives MOH advice for healthy and vulnerable groups, including guidance on N95 masks and PM2.5 bands, and points to the Haze Subsidy Scheme.

title: Haze Subsidy Scheme to start at Public Health Preparedness Clinics and polyclinics from 12 October 2026
summary: The press release says who is eligible for subsidised care of haze-related conditions, the fee caps of 0, 5 and 10 Singapore dollars, and the conditions covered.

title: Ambient (outdoor) air pollution
summary: The fact sheet says exposure to tiny airborne particles outdoors harms the heart and lungs and is linked to an estimated 4.2 million early deaths worldwide in 2019.

title: Wildfires
summary: The fact sheet says wildfire smoke can degrade air quality across wide areas and advises people to follow local guidance, limit time outdoors and keep indoor air clean.

title: Nasihat Kesihatan Mencegah Kemudaratan Jerebu (Health advice to prevent harm from haze, Malay)
summary: The Malay-language page, a 2010 ministry statement, advises reducing outdoor activity, staying indoors where possible, wearing a suitable mask outside and seeing a clinician if symptoms worsen.

publisher: Department of Occupational Safety and Health Malaysia, hosted by Department of Environment Malaysia
title: Guidelines for the Protection of Employees Against the Effects of Haze at Workplaces
summary: The guidelines say that at an API above 100 employers should assess risks, identify susceptible employees and decide when outdoor work stops.
